# University of Sydney Summary
The University of Sydney, established in 1850, is Australia's oldest university and was among the first in the world to admit students regardless of religious or social background, including women on an equal basis since 1881. Its main campus in Camperdown/Darlington features iconic Gothic and Tudor Revival architecture, with ongoing heritage conservation and significant recent upgrades such as new teaching and health buildings. The university comprises eight faculties (including Arts and Social Sciences, Law, Medicine and Health, Science, Engineering, Business, Architecture, and Music) and operates multiple satellite campuses and specialized facilities across Sydney and regional areas. The University Library, with 11 branches and over 5 million items, is the largest academic library in the Southern Hemisphere, and the Chau Chak Wing Museum houses important collections of antiquities, natural history, and art.
The university is highly ranked globally (QS 25th, THE 53rd, ARWU 72nd in 2025–26), and is associated with five Nobel laureates, 24 Rhodes Scholars, and many prominent alumni including multiple Australian prime ministers. Student representation is provided by the University of Sydney Students' Representative Council (SRC), the Sydney University Postgraduate Representative Association (SUPRA), and the University of Sydney Union (USU), which organizes clubs and student activities. The institution has faced challenges, including staff underpayment, issues of sexual harassment in residential colleges, and student satisfaction ratings below national averages in recent years. It maintains a wide range of residential accommodation, with initiatives to support Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander students, and offers substantial research opportunities and funding through endowments and bequests.
